concepts.learning_objective: Define carbohydrates chemically and classify them as monosaccharides, oligosaccharides and polysaccharides by their behaviour on hydrolysis.
Name monosaccharides as aldoses or ketoses by carbon number and recognise that all monosaccharides are reducing sugars.
Relate the reactions of glucose to the evidence for its open-chain structure.
Explain the cyclic hemiacetal (pyranose) structure of glucose and its alpha and beta anomers.
Interpret the D/L and (+)/(-) notation of sugars with reference to glyceraldehyde.

topics.title: Disaccharides, polysaccharides and importance of carbohydrates

concepts.learning_objective: Describe glycosidic linkages in sucrose, maltose and lactose and decide whether a disaccharide is reducing.
Explain the change in sign of rotation on hydrolysis of sucrose (invert sugar).
Compare the structures of starch (amylose, amylopectin), cellulose and glycogen.

topics.title: Amino acids and structure of proteins

concepts.learning_objective: Classify amino acids as acidic, basic or neutral and as essential or non-essential.
Explain the zwitter ion form and the salt-like, amphoteric behaviour of amino acids.
Describe peptide bond formation and the primary to quaternary levels of protein structure.
Explain denaturation of proteins and its effect on their structure and activity.
Describe enzymes as specific biocatalysts that lower activation energy, and how they are named.
Classify vitamins as fat soluble or water soluble and relate this to their storage in the body.
Match important vitamins with their sources and deficiency diseases.
State the sugars, bases and phosphate units of DNA and RNA and distinguish nucleosides from nucleotides.
Apply complementary base pairing in the DNA double helix.
Describe the roles of DNA and RNA in heredity and protein synthesis.
Classify hormones as steroids, polypeptides or amino acid derivatives.
Relate common hormones and glands to their functions and to disorders of deficiency or excess.
